pages.text: "I'll eat quickly and plant again!" Yuki ran from the garden and grabbed a rice ball. Dark soil covered their fingers. Grandma asked about their hands, but Yuki kept eating, pretending not to hear.
"One more seed row and the garden will be full!" Rice still in their mouth, Yuki grabbed another bite with dirty hands. Grandma filled the yard basin.
Soon Yuki's tummy gurgled. "Oh, my tummy..." Yuki curled up on the porch. The seed bag still lay in the garden.
Grandma sat Yuki before the basin. "Lots of things too small to see live in soil. They get onto the rice ball and into your tummy." Yuki stared at the water.
"One, splash your hands in!" Grandma dipped Yuki's hands. Clear water grew cloudy. "Wow, all that came from my hands?"
"Two, make bubbles!" Yuki rubbed both palms hard. Fluffy bubbles covered their hands. "Like mountain fog! Splash Muddy Hands, Clean Hands!"
"Three, scrub between the fingers!" Yuki rubbed this way and that. Fresh rinse water carried away the dirt. "Splash Muddy Hands, Clean Hands!"
Yuki dried their hands on a towel across their knees. Even the fingertips were clean and bright. Their tummy no longer hurt. Brown dog Momo came to nuzzle a palm.
The next day, Yuki stood at the basin first. "Hands before food! One, splash! Two, bubbles! Three, between the fingers!" The water was already cloudy. Yuki tied the scarf knot firmly.

On Grandma's lap, Yuki showed both clean hands. Grandma softly stroked their backs. Eating with hands washed free of dirt kept Yuki's tummy from hurting. Looking at the seed bag by the porch's edge, Yuki said, "Splash Muddy Hands, Clean Hands!"
